title: H10 Holdout: giving up on a question, narrowing it, changing subject, sending again and coming back
capability: Holdout counterpart of the cancel-and-recover class, against a real model. While an answer is still being prepared the person gives up on it (twice, at different moments), narrows the question, moves to another subject, re-sends, loses the connection and comes back. A narrowed question is answered as narrowed; an abandoned answer never arrives late; nothing is stored twice; and a reply that was cut off never becomes a successful Assistant Event.

allowed.statement: Two people cycled with the person: a colleague and that colleague's daughter, who had a flat tyre almost at once.
The decision about the car repair, not the outing, is what weighs on the person right now.

forbidden.statement: Retelling the downpour on the second day and the lift back in a van when only the companions were asked for.
Carrying on with the abandoned answer about the outing after the person moved on to the car repair.
Describing the interruption in system terms such as retries, streams or lookups.

expectedBehavior: After the first cancel, answer the narrowed question about companions only.
After the second cancel and the change of subject, stay with the worry about the repair.
A re-sent message, before or after a restart, resolves to the original and generates nothing new.
Cancelled replies leave no committed Assistant Event.
failureSignals: An assistant reply appears in history for a cancelled turn.
A re-sent message is stored or answered twice.
The narrowed question is ignored and the whole outing is retold.
The reply to the change of subject goes back to the outing.

sourceEligibility.reason: Recent original expression; names the companions.
Recent original expression of the other worry.

criteria.description: Nothing is committed for the first abandoned question.
The narrowed question streams and commits.
History holds the narrowed question once, followed by exactly its reply.
The message naming the companions reaches the Provider.
Nothing is committed for the second abandoned question.
History holds the change of subject once, followed by exactly its reply.
Sending the same message again is idempotent.
Sending it again after a restart is idempotent.
The conversation carries on normally after the restart.
Response-time contract for the narrowed question.
Response-time contract for the change of subject.
Response-time contract for the first turn after a restart (cold).

After the change of subject the reply stays with the new subject.
